newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Vaa l buys SAfrican gold mine Weltevreden.
newsitem.headline: Vaa l buys SAfrican gold mine Weltevreden.

text.p: South African mining firm Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co Ltd said on Friday that it had bought control of Weltevreden Mines Ltd by acquiring Gengold's 76.6 percent stake in the firm.

Vaal Reefs said it had sealed the deal by acquiring certain mineral rights in the southern Free State and Evander areas from Anglo American Corp and Anglo American Gold Investment and exchanging them for Weltevreden.
Vaal Reefs paid for the mineral rights with 416,400 Vaal shares.
The Weltevreden ore body varies in depth from 100 metres to 900 metres below the surface and Vaal Reefs said it intends to extend a tribute agreement to the acquired firm.
This will see Vaal Reefs mine the area, receive 55 percent of revenue and pay 55 percent of the costs. The remaining 45 percent will accrue to Weltevreden.

The Weltevreden area will be mined from Vaal Reef's Number Ten Shaft. The firm estimates the area will yield at least 10.6 million milled tons at an average grade of 6.4 grams a ton, resulting in 2.2 million ounces of gold being produced over 17 years starting in 1998.
Capital costs are estimated at 221 million rand.
Vaal Reefs is also talking to Amgold and Anglo about the Area One East mining resource, but said further evaluations needed to be done before any mining plan could be worked out.
